title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
description:
Given an array of non-negative integers `heights` representing the heights of bars in a histogram where the width of each bar is `1`, return the area of the largest axis-aligned rectangle that can be formed completely inside the histogram.

A rectangle spanning contiguous bars `[l, r]` has width `r - l + 1` and maximum possible height `min(heights[l], heights[l + 1], ..., heights[r])`.
hints: Any maximal rectangle is bounded in height by at least one bar `i`. Its maximum width extends left to the nearest shorter bar and right to the nearest shorter bar.
Maintain a monotonic increasing stack of bar indices. When a shorter bar arrives at index `i`, every taller bar popped from the stack has `i` as its right boundary.
After popping index `idx`, the new stack top (or `-1` if empty) is its left boundary, giving width `i - left - 1`. Append a sentinel `0` height at the end to flush remaining bars.

examples.explanation: Bars at indices 2 and 3 (heights 5 and 6) form a rectangle of height 5 and width 2, giving area 10.
A rectangle of height 2 spanning both bars has area 2 * 2 = 4, equal to the single bar of height 4.
The single bar of height 9 forms a rectangle of area 9.
